## Set-up {#sec-ot-setup}

The three-dimensionally perturbed Orszag–Tang vortex of @sec-conservation runs on a 3-level nest:
a periodic $32^3$ root and two $32^3$ children, each covering the central half of its parent
(effective resolution $128^3$ in the central $1/4^3$ of the box). Both $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$
treatments, HLL, `Float64`, Courant 0.4, to $t = 0.5$, with snapshots every $\Delta t = 0.05$. The
field is set from the vector potential
$\mathbf A = \big(0,\ 0.2\,B_0 x,\ B_0[\cos 4\pi x/4\pi + \cos 2\pi y/2\pi]\big)$, $B_0 = 1/\sqrt{4\pi}$.

## The run {#sec-ot-run}

```{=html}
<div class="qd-widget" data-widget="ot"></div>
```

The left panel composites the $z$-midplane of all three levels, with the finest data drawn on top
(outlines mark the patches). The shocks and current sheets cross both refinement boundaries. At
this resolution (32 cells per patch) no artefacts are visible along the patch edges. That is a
qualitative statement; the quantitative interface tests are in @sec-ghost. In the log-scale panels,
values that are exactly zero are drawn at $10^{-17}$.

- **Conservation.** Total mass and energy stay at $|\Delta m/m| \le 3.8\times10^{-16}$ and
  $|\Delta E/E| \le 1.6\times10^{-16}$ throughout, in both modes.
- **CT.** $\max|\nabla\cdot\mathbf B|\,\Delta x/\max|\mathbf B|$ stays between $1.5\times10^{-15}$ and
  $6\times10^{-15}$ on every level for the whole run.
- **GLM.** The same measure fluctuates between $5\times10^{-2}$ and $6\times10^{-1}$. It is bounded, but
  not zero, and larger than on a uniform grid ($2$–$6\times10^{-2}$ for the 2-D problem at $t=0.2$ in @sec-otref).
- **Steps.** The levels take 255 / 522 / 1062 steps (CT) and 298 / 795 / 1521 (GLM; the
  two runs evolve differently, so their CFL steps differ): about two per parent step on the root,
  up to 2.7 where the shocks steepen. Each count is the one that level's CFL condition
  requires, not a fixed ratio.
